name: Bloomy-rind soft cheese (generic)
definition: white-mould soft cheese sold as soft-ripened cheese or under a name with no kind of its own (Chaource, Neufchâtel, Brillat-Savarin); not brie or camembert.
notes: Chaource PDO sold as bloomy-rind soft cheese, pasteurised cow milk, France

name: Lactic soft-ripened cheese (crottin type)
definition: small soft cheese of slow acid-set (lactic) curd, mostly goat's milk, ripened with a natural, geotrichum, mould or ash rind (crottin, Sainte-Maure, Valençay, Picodon, Saint-Marcellin).
notes: Sainte-Maure de Touraine goat cheese, ashed thin soft rind, listed by UK retailer (sold out)

name: Sour-milk cheese (Harzer, Handkäse)
definition: small cheese of ripened acid curd (quark), ripened with a smear or mould to a translucent, pungent body (Harzer, Handkäse, Olomoucké tvarůžky, Graukäse, gamalost).
notes: Olomoucke tvaruzky sold: ripened washed-rind cheese; Poelmeyer sells Harzer sour-milk cheese brands

name: Colby
definition: mild, moist, washed-curd semi-hard cheese of the American type, often orange.
notes: Widmer Natural Colby: mild, moist, washed-curd, semi-hard, sold; USDA standard defines Colby

name: Monterey Jack
definition: mild, pale, semi-soft to semi-hard pressed cheese of the Californian type, aged to dry Jack.
notes: Cabot Monterey Jack block sold in US groceries; USDA standard; cow milk, mild

name: Fontina
definition: semi-hard, supple washed-rind cow's-milk cheese of the Aosta type, melting well (Fontina DOP; Danish and US fontina).
notes: Wisconsin (Stella) and Danish fontina listed outside Aosta; no DOP; semi-soft cow milk

name: Asiago
definition: pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Asiago type, fresh (pressato) or aged (d'allevo).
notes: BelGioioso Aged Asiago wedge sold, made in Wisconsin

name: Tilsit
definition: semi-hard smear-ripened cheese with small holes, of the Tilsit type.
notes: Tilsiter offered for sale: semi-hard, small irregular holes, thin rind, cow milk
